- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10) and price is trending up, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast peak to avoid overshoot.  
- Model consistently underestimates price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — adjust downward bias by 0.5–1.5% for such cases.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 7-day avg), model often overreacts in next 3–5 days — apply “lag correction” by reducing forecast by 1–3% for 3–5 days post-spike.  
- Mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 1–2% for next 5 days unless sentiment strongly bullish.  
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.3 to -0.2) triggers “reversion trigger” — model often misses correction — reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–7 days.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, model tends to underestimate price when sentiment is weak or neutral — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment < 0.05 over last 5 days.
